ladder.kicker: What UC Berkeley actually cares about
ladder.title: Only 3 things are top-tier. Your PIQs are the one you can still change.
ladder.lede: By senior fall, your classes and GPA are mostly set. Your essays, which UC calls Personal Insight Questions (PIQs), are the top-tier piece you can still change before Nov 30.
considered: First in your family to go to college
not_considered: How often you toured or emailed
ladder.note: Top tier = where your hours go before Nov 30 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set. C7 marks test scores "considered," but C8 says Berkeley doesn't use SAT or ACT scores in admission, so they're listed as not considered here. Letters: C8F says Berkeley only considers them when it asks for them.

numbers.lede: Type your GPA on a 4.0 scale to see where it sits next to Berkeley's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.default: Average GPA of enrolled first-years: 3.9 on a 4.0 scale.
gpa.near: Right around Berkeley's average. Now your top-tier rows decide it: how hard your classes were, and your PIQs.
gpa.above: Above Berkeley's average. Good start. Your classes and PIQs still do the heavy lifting.
gpa.below: Below Berkeley's average. That's not a no. Your PIQs are top-tier too, and they're the piece you can still change. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of enrolled first-years had a GPA of 3.75 or higher (40% had a 4.0).

money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. The net price calculator gives your family a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: About 4 in 10 first-years get need-based grants. First-years who got aid averaged $39,656 a year.

todo.title: 4 moves, all aimed at Berkeley's top tier.

items.title: Read your 4 PIQs in one sitting.
items.body: PIQs are top-tier here. If two tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

items.title: Check your courses against your transcript.
items.body: The UC application has you type in every class and grade yourself. Match it line by line. Your classes and GPA are top-tier.

items.title: Pick your first-choice major on purpose.
items.body: Berkeley only reviews your first-choice major. It won't review your alternate. Business (Haas) is all or nothing: if you're not admitted to the major, you're not admitted to Berkeley.

items.title: Line up 2 people for a letter, just in case.
items.body: Berkeley invites some applicants to send letters after they apply. One should be an academic teacher. Ask now, so you're ready if the email comes.

todo.done: All 4 done. That's a real application. ✓

title.s: Are your PIQs doing their job?
title.p: Are your student's PIQs doing their job?

lede.s: PIQs are top-tier at UC Berkeley. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your PIQs together, then tap what's true.
lede.p: PIQs are top-tier at UC Berkeley. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your student's PIQs together, then tap what's true.

items.title: Each one answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the question. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only you could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows what you did.
items.body: Your role, your steps, what changed. Not just what the team or club did.

items.title: The 4 show 4 different sides of you.
items.body: If two PIQs tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own writing.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge writing you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: When 9 out of 10 first-years have a 3.75 or higher, your grades get you read. They don't get you picked. Your PIQs are where the reader finds a reason to fight for you. Give them one real story per question.
